pr.title: Star items and show only the starred ones

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_starred.sql adds starred NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 with CHECK. test/starred.test.js 'AC-1' checks all seeded rows are 0 and that a value of 2 is rejected.
test 'AC-2' checks the exact list contents: only the starred item has ★ before its title.
test 'AC-3' stars ids 3 and 1 and checks the starred view lists them in id order with a 200.
test 'AC-4' checks / and /?show=all both list all items in id order.

AC-5 as it now reads requires the link 'Most items' on the starred list. The code (VIEWS.starred.link) and the test emit and assert 'All items'. The code matches the original AC-5 wording, but the late commit 691bb1a changed the item without a recorded owner decision, so the shipped behaviour departs from the spec as written.
test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for Starred, none, empty and __proto__. The code uses Object.hasOwn.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?show=starred'. test 'AC-7' asserts it. traffic-config-check accepts it, and tests/traffic-config.test.sh covers that.

findings.what: Commit 691bb1a ('Follow-up edits', a github-actions bot commit) changed AC-5 from 'All items' to 'Most items' after the go. No decision in the spec records an owner call or date. The Core flow and States table still say 'All items', so the spec now contradicts itself, and the code and tests ('All items') no longer match AC-5.
findings.fix: Revert the AC-5 edit to 'All items', or get a dated owner decision recording the rename and update the code, tests, Core flow and States table together.

findings.what: The PR says 'Changed after the go: nothing', but the final commit edits acceptance item AC-5 after the go.
findings.fix: Disclose the AC-5 change under 'Changed after the go', or revert it.

findings.what: The AC-5 test asserts 'All items', which contradicts the spec's current AC-5 text ('Most items'). The test is not evidence for AC-5 as written.
findings.fix: Resolve the spec wording first, then align the test.

lenses.note: A spec exists. The late AC-5 edit departs from the go, and no decision records it.
AC-5 is unmet as written. The other items are met. All four state-table rows have tests.
Tests assert behaviour and would fail on broken code. The vitest suite was not run here; CI runs it. The traffic fakeApp change is a legitimate extension, not a loosening.
The README describes ?show=starred. No other docs are stale.
The query is a fixed template with no user input. Object.hasOwn guards __proto__. No defects found.
No injection risk. Titles are escaped, and show is validated against an allowlist. The route-regex relaxation still refuses spaces and #.
The diff touches only a minimal server-rendered HTML string, with no UI/style files.
The diff touches no UI flow files beyond the plain HTML list, and the PR gives no preview.
'Changed after the go: nothing' is false because of the AC-5 edit. The other claims check out.
